methodology: Direct file read — content block (Part, Section, Topic, Stem, Choices.{A,B,C,D}, CorrectChoice, ExplanationCorrect) compared against metadata block (ExplanationWrongA-D, question_state) within same JSON object per QuestionID. Each EW field evaluated for topic alignment (does EW text describe this item's concept area?) and choice specificity (does EW text address the specific Choice.{letter} text?).
dual_block_note: Pack A uses single-object-per-QID architecture (not dual-block like Pack C/D). Content fields (Topic, Stem, Choices, CC, EC) and metadata fields (EW-A-D, question_state) are in the SAME JSON object. DL-016 in this context means EW text within the object describes a different item's topic or template-level choices that diverge from the actual Choices.{letter} values.

items.analysis_notes: MAJOR DL-016 RESIDUE. Item topic is budgetary slack / incentive design. ALL THREE distractor EW fields describe FORECASTING ERROR ANALYSIS (P1-B-026's topic), not budgetary slack at all. EW-A talks about 'abandoning forecasting because actual results differ from forecasts' — this describes forecast error analysis, not budgetary slack. EW-B describes 'Not every forecast error indicates fraud' — forecasting, not budgetary slack. EW-C describes 'Selecting only the best-performing month discards the other 11 months' — forecasting evaluation, not budgetary slack. The EW texts are near-verbatim copies of P1-B-026's EW fields (with slightly different wording). This is the classic DL-016 +1 shift: the metadata block was written for P1-B-026's topic but placed in P1-B-025's object.

ew_fields_check.notes: DL-016 RESIDUE: CC=A, so EW-A should be empty. It is NOT empty. EW-A says 'Abandoning forecasting because actual results differ from forecasts misunderstands the fundamental purpose of forecasting in management accounting. All forecasts inherently contain error...' This is about forecasting, NOT budgetary slack. Choice A is 'Revise incentives and review assumptions to discourage slack while preserving accountability.' Complete topic mismatch. Additionally, this slot should be EMPTY (CC slot), confirming a DL-008 violation as well.

DL-016 RESIDUE: EW-B says 'Not every forecast error indicates fraud. Errors arise from many legitimate sources: changes in market conditions, data limitations, model misspecification, or random variation.' This is about forecasting, NOT budgetary slack. Choice B is 'Eliminate all variance analysis from the budget process.' Complete topic mismatch.

DL-016 RESIDUE: EW-C says 'Selecting only the best-performing month discards the other 11 months of data, creating a cherry-picked and unreliable assessment of forecast performance.' This is about forecast error evaluation, NOT budgetary slack. Choice C is 'Classify slack as a cash equivalent.' Complete topic mismatch.

EW-D is empty (''). This is the CC slot that should be empty — but CorrectChoice IS A, not D. So EW-D empty while EW-A should be empty. This confirms the EW fields are shifted: they belong to P1-B-026 (CC=D) where EW-D is the correct empty CC slot.

residue_items.pattern: EW-C and EW-D describe budget sequencing concepts (cash budget timing, direct materials budget) that do not match the actual Choices C (tax return first) or D (budgeted balance sheet first). EW texts appear to originate from template-level choices that were changed in the final item.

All three distractor EW fields (A, B, C) describe P1-B-026's forecast error analysis topic, not P1-B-025's budgetary slack topic. Classic DL-016 +1 shift: the metadata block EW text was written for P1-B-026 and placed in P1-B-025. Additionally, EW-A is non-empty despite CorrectChoice=A — this is also a DL-008 violation (non-empty EW at CC slot).

findings.P1_B_008: EW-C and EW-D describe template-level choices (cash budget positioning, direct materials budget sequencing) that do not match the actual item choices (tax return first, budgeted balance sheet first). The EW text is on-topic for budget sequencing but describes different specific choices than what the item renders. Template divergence.
findings.P1_B_025: Complete +1 shift: all EW fields belong to P1-B-026 (forecast error analysis). Items B-025 and B-026 appear to share the same rotation group. P1-B-025 is the CC=A item with EW fields from the CC=D template slot. The empty EW-D in B-025 (should be empty since CC=A) confirms the shift — D is the correct empty slot for P1-B-026 (CC=D). P1-B-025 also carries a DL-008 violation: EW-A is non-empty while CorrectChoice=A.

summary.rotation_group_analysis: Items B-021 through B-025 form a 5-item rotation group (expected value, regression, learning curve, cash budget borrowing, budgetary slack). P1-B-025 is the last seed in this group. Items B-026 through B-030 form the next 5-item group (forecast error, budget committee, continuous planning, production budget 13, materials purchases 14). P1-B-026 is the first seed in its group. The DL-016 shift at B-025→B-026 boundary suggests the rotation template assigned EW text across group boundaries.
summary.certified_impact: Both DL-016 residue items (P1-B-008, P1-B-025) are Certified and in the learner delivery pool. P1-B-025 additionally has a DL-008 violation (non-empty EW-A at CC=A slot). Educational impact: learners who select wrong answers on B-008 choices C/D and B-025 choices A/B/C see feedback about unrelated topics.
